story.introduction: Introduction

points.text: Musa (a.s) was from the descendants of Ibraheem (a.s), Ishaaq (a.s) and Yaqoob (a.s) and therefore belongs to the clan of Bani Israel or the Children of Israel. The Firaun (Pharaoh or King) who ruled Egypt at that time was a tyrant who oppressed the Bani Israel. He used every means to demean and disgrace the Bani Israel and forced them to worship him as god and to carry out his orders.

As years passed, the Bani Israel multiplied to a larger number. One day, the Firaun had a vision in which a fire comes from Jerusalem and burns the houses of the Egyptians, but does not harm the Children of Israel. He woke up horrified and called all his priests and courtiers and asked them about his vision. They interpreted the vision saying that a boy will be born from the Bani Israel and the Egyptians will perish at his hands.

The Firaun immediately commanded that henceforth all male children being born among the children of Israel shall be killed. The order was carried out for some time until some of his courtiers dealing in the economics of the land came to Firaun with a problem. They said that the aged among the Bani Israel are dying, and if the infants continue to get slaughtered, there will be no more manpower for them to extract work from. They suggested that a policy be made wherein the males are slaughtered in one year and spared to live the next year. The Firaun found this solution to be safer economically and therefore had it implemented.

Musa’s mother was pregnant with Haroon in a year that boys were to be spared. Thus she gave birth to Haroon publicly and safely. She gave birth to Musa during the year where boys were to be slain, so she kept herself inside of her house and bore Musa in secret and nursed him in hiding. Allah inspired the mother of Musa to cast him in the river Nile and the story relating to the childhood and youth of Musa (a.s) are beautifully captured in Surah Al-Qasas and summarised below:

verses.text: Allah narrates to you some information about Musa and Firaun for the believers.
Firaun elevated himself in the land and oppressed one group of people, putting their sons to death and sparing only their females. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 1)
Allah wanted to favor those who were oppressed, to make them leaders and make them inheritors of the land. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 1)

Allah inspired the mother of Musa to suckle him and cast him into the river (on a basket) without any grief, for Allah shall restore Musa back to her and make him a Rasool. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 1)

Allah made Firaun’s family to pick him up from the river. The wife of Firaun said: “This child may become the comfort of the eyes for me and for you (i.e Firaun). Do not kill him. He may prove useful to us or it may be that we will adopt him as our son”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 1)
(She pleaded so much that Firaun agreed to spare baby Musa, and it was as per the plan and will of Allah that Musa will be raised in the palaces of Firaun)

Musa’s sister came to Firaun’s wife and said: “Shall I point out to you a house whose people will take care of him for you and they will be sincere to him?” Thus Allah restored Musa to his mother, so she may be comforted and that she might know that the promise of Allah is true. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 1)
When Musa reached maturity and full strength, Allah bestowed on him wisdom and knowledge. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)

One day, Musa entered the city and found two people fighting. One was from his own race (an Israelite) and the other was an Egyptian. The Israelite called upon Musa for help, whereupon Musa gave his foe a blow that killed him (accidentally and without intending his death). (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)

Musa realized that this was from the work of Shaitan and he prayed to Allah for forgiveness. So Allah forgave him and Musa said: “O my Rabb! After this favor that You have bestowed on me, I shall never be a helping hand to the criminals.” (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)

The next morning, he saw the same man (from the Israelite) whom he had helped the previous day and the man cried out to Musa for help to save him from another Egyptian. Musa told him: “You are certainly a misguided person”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)
Then when Musa was about to lay his hands on him, he called out: “O Musa! Do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday”? (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)
(News spread about Musa having killed an Egyptian) and a man came running to Musa saying that the chiefs were plotting to kill him. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)
Musa left the land (immediately) in fear and caution, praying: “O my Rabb! Deliver me from the nation of wrongdoers”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 2)

Musa made his way towards Madyan, and when he arrived to the well of Madyan, he saw two women who were holding their flock back, while waiting for the men to finish watering their flock. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 3)
Musa helped the women to water their flock and went back to the shade and prayed “O my Rabb! Surely I am in desperate need of whatever good that You may send down to me”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 3)
Soon after that, one of the women came to Musa saying: “My father is calling you. He wishes to reward you for watering our flocks for us”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 3)
Musa came to him and narrated his story. The old man (it is believed to be Shuaib a.s) said: “Have no fear. You have escaped from those wicked people”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 3)

The old man then offered one of his daughters in marriage to Musa if he would stay in service for a minimum of 8 years, but if he can make it 10 years, it would be gracious of him. Musa agreed to this proposal (and settled in Madyan for some time). (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 3)

story.introduction: Introduction

points.text: The Story of Musa from the time he departed from Madyan with his family and up to the competition with magicians is captured below. (Aayahs from Surah Ta-ha, Al-Qasas and Al-A’raf have been combined to keep the flow of the story and timeline.)

story.introduction: Allah speaks to Musa (a.s) in the valley of Tuwa

verses.text: Have you heard the story of Musa (O Prophet s.a.w.s)? While on a journey with his family, he found himself lost. He then saw a fire at some distance. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 1)
When he reached there, Allah called out: “O Musa! In fact, I am your Rabb! Take off your shoes, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.” (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 1)
News is given of Musa being chosen and appointed as a Prophet. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 1)

Allah then shows some of the signs that He would give to Musa. Allah asks him to throw down his staff. Musa throws it down and it becomes a snake, active in motion. Allah asks him to catch it and not to be afraid. It will change back to its original shape. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 1)
Allah then asks him to put his hand under his armpit and it shall become shining white. Musa is then asked to go to Firaun with these signs. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 1)

Musa prays: “O my Rabb! Open my heart, ease my task and remove the impediment from my speech”. Musa requests that Allah grant him his brother Haroon as a minister to strengthen him. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 2)

Allah grants Musa his request. Allah then reminds Musa about the favor he bestowed on him earlier, when Allah inspired Musa’s mother to put him (when he was a child), in a basket and throw it into the river. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 2)
The river cast the basket on to the banks and the child was picked up by Firaun’s family, who adopted him. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 2)
Then through Musa’s sister, Allah got her to inform Firaun’s wife about a woman who can take care of the child. Thus Allah got Musa back to his mother. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 2)

Allah then says that Musa and his brother should go to Firaun with His Signs, for Firaun has transgressed all bounds. They should speak to him in gentle words and to mention Allah. They should ask that he let the Children of Israel go with them and not to oppress them. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 2)

Musa reveals his fear that he had killed a man, and the people would put him to death. He also requests Allah to send his brother Haroon with him, as he was more eloquent in speech. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 4)

Allah says: “We will certainly strengthen you with your brother and give both of you such authority that they shall not be able to harm you. With Our signs you two as well as those who follow you will surely triumph”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 4)

story.introduction: Musa (a.s) and Haroon (a.s) go to Firaun

verses.text: Musa and Haroon go to Firaun and deliver the message. When Firaun asks: “Well; who is your Rabb O Musa?”, Musa replies: “Our Rabb is He Who has given a distinctive form to all creatures and then rightly guided them.” (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 2)
Musa shows the signs to Firaun, and Firaun calls it a magic, plotted to drive the people out of the land. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 3)
Firaun then challenges Musa to a contest to match his magic, and the Day of Festival is fi xed for the challenge between Musa and the magicians of the kingdom. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 3)
The magicians arrived and asked Firaun about their reward if they prevail over Musa. Firaun promised them not only reward but a higher rank amongst his chiefs. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 14)

The magicians came to Musa and asked who will cast fi rst and Musa asked them to cast fi rst. Th e magicians made a mighty display of sorcery which enchanted the eyes of the people and frightened them. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 14)

Allah comforts Musa to not be afraid and that he will surely come out on top. Musa then throws down his staff  and it becomes a serpent swallowing up all the magic that was produced. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 3)

The magicians (being professionals) realize that this was not magic but a miracle. So they humble themselves by prostrating and say, “We believe in the Rabb of Haroon and Musa”. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 3)
Firaun becomes furious and says that he would cut off  their hands and feet from either side, and crucify them on the trunks of palm trees. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 3)
The magicians reply that they can never prefer Firaun over the miracle that they have witnessed. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 3)
The magicians remained steadfast and prayed to Allah: “O our Rabb! Pour upon us patience and make us die as Muslims”. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 14)

story.introduction: Introduction

points.text: After defeating the magicians, Musa and Haroon left the palace of Firaun. The people had witnessed a clear victory for Musa and more and more people started following him. Firaun was furious with this development and was in violent rage. He knew that he had to stop this movement at any cost. After his anger calmed down, he called all the ministers, leaders and responsible men to discuss how Musa should be stopped.

The conversations at the meetings are captured below from aayahs of Surah Al Mu’min & Surah Al Qasas. The punishments that Allah sent upon the people of Egypt and the plight of those following Musa are captured below from Surah Al-A’raf, Az Zukhruf and Surah Yunus.

story.introduction: Discussions at the palace of Firaun

verses.text: Allah sent Musa a.s with His signs and clear authority to Firaun, Haman and Qaroon, but they called him a sorcerer and a liar. (Surah Al-Mu’min : Section 3)

When Musa had brought to them the truth from Allah, they said “Kill the sons of those who share their faith with Musa, and leave only their females.” But futile were the schemes of the unbelievers. (Surah Al-Mu’min : Section 3)
Finally Firaun said: “Let me kill Musa; and let him invoke his Rabb! I fear that he may change your religion or that he may cause mischief to appear in the land”. (Surah Al-Mu’min : Section 3)

One of the believers (a Mu’min) from among the relatives of Firaun, who had kept his faith a secret, said: “Will you kill a man (i.e Musa) merely because he says: ‘My Rabb is Allah’; and who has brought you clear signs from your Rabb”. (Surah Al-Mu’min : Section 4)

One of the believers (a Mu’min) from among the relatives of Firaun, who had kept his faith a secret, said: “Will you kill a man (i.e Musa) merely because he says: ‘My Rabb is Allah’; and who has brought you clear signs from your Rabb”. (Surah Al-Mu’min : Section 4)

The Mu’min further warned, “O my people! I fear for you the day of disaster like what befell the prior people, such as the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud and those who came after them”. (Surah Al-Mumin : Section 4)

Firaun said: “O Chiefs! You have no other god that I know of, except myself”. Then turning to (one of his chief) Ha’man, he said: “O Ha’man! Bake for me bricks from clay and build a high tower, so that I may climb it to see the God of Musa. Most surely, I think him to be one of the liars.” (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 4)
Thus Firaun’s evil deeds were made fair seeming to him and he turned away from the Right Way. The scheme of Firaun led him to nothing but destruction. (Surah Al-Mumin : Section 4)

story.introduction: Allah’s punishment on the people of Egypt
story.text: Upon hearing that Firaun was planning further torture and persecution upon the followers of Musa,

verses.text: Musa said to his people “Seek help from Allah and be patient. The land belongs to Allah. He gives it as a heritage to those of His servants whom He pleases. You should know that final success is for the righteous.” (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 15).

Allah then commanded Musa (a.s) to tell the Firan that the Egyptians will suffer a severe punishment if he does not release the children of Israel. The Firaun still was in denial. Allah then afflicted the people of Firaun with severe draught and other punishments
Allah afflicted Firaun’s people with several years of famine and shortage of fruit so that they might come to their senses. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 16)
Allah sent upon them the floods, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs and the blood; yet they remained persistent in their arrogance. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 16)

Every time the plague fell, Firaun’s people came to Musa asking him to pray to his Rabb on their behalf and promised that if Musa will help remove the plague, they will truly believe in him and send the Children of Israel with him. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 16)
But every time Allah removed the plague, they broke their promise. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 16)
(This scene is captured in Surah Az Zukhruf along with conversations among the people)

Allah had sent Musa (a.s) with His signs to Firaun and his chiefs. But they laughed at him. Yet Allah showed them sign after signs through Musa, each one greater than the other. (Surah AzZukhruf :Section 5)
Each time they were seized by the scourge, the people requested to Musa, “O magician! Pray to your Rabb for us, we shall surely accept your guidance”. (Surah Az-Zukhruf :Section 5)
But each time Allah lifted the scourge from them, they broke their pledge. (Surah Az-Zukhruf :Section 5)

(One day), Firaun made a proclamation to his people asking “Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine. Are these rivers flowing beneath me not mine also? Can you not see? Am I not better than this despicable wretch (Musa), who can hardly express himself clearly?” (Surah Az-Zukhruf :Section 5)
Firaun continued: “If he is really a Rasool, then why have no gold bracelets been given to him, or angels sent down to accompany him?” (Surah Az-Zukhruf :Section 5)
Thus, Firaun misled his people and they obeyed him. Surely, they were a nation of transgressors. (Surah Az-Zukhruf :Section 5)

story.introduction: Plight of the people of Musa
story.text: Musa kept giving hope to his people and asking them to trust and believe in Allah. Firaun had made their daily existence difficult and the people used to ask Musa:

verses.text: “We were oppressed before you came to us and since you have come to us”. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 15).

Musa said: “O my people! If you believe in Allah, then put your trust in Him, if you are really Muslims”. The people replied: “In Allah do we put our trust. Our Rabb! Do not let us suffer at the hands of unjust people and deliver us through Your mercy, from the nation of unbelievers”. (Surah Yunus : Section 9)

Allah revealed to Musa and his brother to tell their people, to make their houses as place of worship (since Firaun had prohibited public prayers) and establish prayer (in their homes) and give good news to the believers. (Surah Yunus : Section 9)
Musa (a.s) prayed to Allah to destroy the wealth of Firaun and his chiefs, and harden their hearts, so that they may not believe until they see the painful punishment. (Surah Yunus : Section 9)
Little did Firaun and his people know that their doom was very near.

story.text: Before we go to the incident of Musa departing Egypt with the children of Israel, we will go over some incidents that happened in Egypt – two of which are referenced in the Quran and one, which is from a hadith.

story.introduction: Incident of Qaroon

verses.text: Qaroon was one of the people of Musa, but he behaved arrogantly towards them. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)
Allah had given him such treasures that their very keys were a burden to a band of strongmen. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)

The people warned Qaroon: “Do not exult, for Allah does not love the exultant”. But Qaroon replied: “All that I have been given is by virtue of the knowledge that I possess”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)

One day, he came out before his people in his worldly glitter. Those who sought the life of this world said: Ah! Would that we had the like of Qaroon’s fortune! He is indeed a very lucky man”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)
The next day, Allah caused the earth to swallow him along with his dwellings, and he had no host to help him against Allah; nor was he able to defend himself. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)

Now the same people who wished for a position like his, the day before, began to say: “Alas! We had forgotten that it is indeed Allah Who enlarges the provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it from whom He pleases”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)

The people continued: “If Allah had not been gracious to us, He could have caused the earth to swallow us too. Alas! We had forgotten that the unbelievers will never be successful”. (Surah Al-Qasas : Section 8)

story.introduction: Incident of the Hairdresser at Firaun’s palace

points.text: A hairdresser was combing the hair of one of Firaun’s daughters when the iron comb fell from her hand and she said, “Bismillah” (in the name of Allah) while picking it up. The daughter of Firaun asked; “You mean my father”. To this she replied, “No, I refer to my Lord and the Lord of your father Who is Allah”.

Firaun’s daughter informed to Firaun about the hairdresser and he was livid with rage. He wanted to make her as an example for his people. He asked for a huge pot to be brought forth and had it filled with oil and boiled it up. He then called the hairdresser along with her children.
She had five children and Firaun started throwing them one by one into the boiling oil while she was made to watch. Finally, it was just her and the baby which was still breastfeeding.

She had a bit of reluctance due to the infant child, but Allah gave her strength and she called to Firaun with a request. She said: “I would li.ke my bones and my children’s bones to be gathered together in one cloth. and be buried together”. Firaun accepted this request and she went. forth into the boiling oil, with her infant child in her hand.

This incident is captured in a hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in Al-Musnad, wherein it is narrated that Ibn Abbas (r.a) said; On the night when the messenger of Allah was taken on the Night Journey (Isra’), a beautiful fragrance came to him. He asked Jibreel (a.s) about this beautiful fragrance and Jibreel said that this fragrance is from the grave of the hairdresser of the Firaun’s daughter and her children.

story.introduction: Wife of Firaun - Asiya bint Muzahim

points.text: Asiya bint Muzahim was the wife of Firaun. She was a very beautiful woman, extremely generous and came from among the rich families of Egypt. Being married to the Firaun, she led a life of luxury and comfort. From an Islamic perspective, her story starts when she was sitting near the Nile river and a small basket comes forth carrying baby Musa (a.s). She had no children and her heart was immediately in love with this baby. She felt so much love for the child, that she pleaded with Firaun saying:

verses.text: “This child may become the comfort of the eyes for me and for you. Do not kill him. He may prove useful to us or it may be that we will adopt him as our son”. (Surah Al-Qasas : 9).

points.text: Musa is then raised in the palace of Firaun and Asiya dedicates herself to raising Musa (a.s) and loves him as her own son.

As time goes on, Musa (a.s) comes to Firaun asking him to believe and worship one Allah. Asiya immediately believes in Musa (a.s). She starts to practice the religion of Musa. Knowing the consequence if Firaun gets to know about her faith, she keeps her conversion a secret.

When the incident of the hairdresser happened, everyone was witness to the exemplary courage shown by the woman and her children. Asiya too found the ability to stand up to her husband and reveal her true beliefs. She came forth to Firaun one evening and told him that she believed in the One true God, she disbelieved in Firaun and did not care about what he would do to her.

Firaun was shocked and he decided to torture Asiya until her resolve weakens. Firaun has Asiya pulled out of the palace and thrown into the burning sands of the Egyptian desert. He has her starved, stripped of her honour and dignity and has her hands and feet pegged with nails. His daughters (from other wives and concubines) laugh at Asiya as she is tortured. Firaun then instructs his soldiers to lash her. While enduring her husband’s punishments, Asiya prays to Allah and the incident is captured in the Quran:

verses.text: And for the believers Allah has set an example in the wife of Firaun, who said: “My Rabb! Build for me a house as a special favour from You in paradise, deliver me from Firaun and his misdeeds, and save me from the wicked nation”. (Surah - At Tahreem : 11).

points.text: In response to her supplication, Allah opened up the skies for her and allowed her to see her place in Jannah. Asiya laughed in joy at this revelation. Firaun said to the people that she has become mad, for she laughs while being humiliated and tortured. He orders that a huge boulder be thrown upon her to kill her, and while the boulder is thrown, Allah orders the soul of Asiya to be removed.

Our Prophet (s.a.w.s) has mentioned in an authentic hadith recorded in Musnad Ahmad that “the best of the women of Paradise are Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Maryam bint Imran and Asiya bint Muzahim, the wife of Firaun”.

story.introduction: Firaun releases the children of Israel and Allah’s command to Musa to set off with his people

points.text: Coming back to our timeline, the people of Egypt are faced with one punishment after another of drought, floods, locusts, lice, frogs and the river Nile turning to blood.

Back in the palace, Firaun eventually gives in and releases the children of Israel. But his actual plan is to attack the people while they are near to the Sea. This incident is captured beautifully in Surah Ash-Shua’ra, along with the emotions and expressions of the people when they saw the army of Firaun coming to attack them.

verses.text: Allah revealed to Musa to set off with his people by night, and cautioned that they will be pursued. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 4)
At sunrise, the Egyptians pursued them (until they reached a place in front of the Red Sea). (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 4)
With the Red Sea in front and Firaun’s army behind them, the companions of Musa cried out: “We are surely overtaken”. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 4)
Musa said, “Not at all! My Rabb is with me; He will show me a way out”. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 4)

Allah revealed to Musa to strike the sea with his staff, and the sea split, each part standing like a mighty mountain. The believers crossed the sea while Firaun and his army followed them. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 4)
Allah delivered Musa and all who were with him; and drowned the others. Surely there is a lesson in this; yet most of these people do not learn and become believers. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 4

story.introduction: Death of Firaun

points.text: Firaun too pursued the Egyptians and entered into the Red Sea. Allah ordered the waters to come back to how they originally were, and Firaun along with his army drowned.

verses.text: While drowning, Firaun cried out: “I believe that there is none worthy of worship but Allah, in Whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am one of the Muslims”. (Surah Yunus : Section 9)
In response, it was said to him: “Now you believe! But a little while before, you were disobedient and one of the mischiefmakers! (Surah Yunus : Section 9)
We shall save your body today, so that you may become a sign for the succeeding generations; indeed, many among mankind are heedless of Our signs!” (Surah Yunus : Section 9).
Thus was the end of Firaun, and his body is still saved today for the people to see how Allah humiliated him and to take heed.

story.introduction: Musa (a.s) and the Children of Israel:

points.text: With the Children of Israel having crossed the Red Sea and the death of Firaun, Allah was going to give something special to Musa (a.s) and his people. Allah commanded Musa to take the Children of Israel to Mount Tur and there, Allah was going to give Musa (a.s) the Tawrat.

The Children of Israel were about six to seven hundred thousand people. While they were heading to Mount Tur, the people got tired and hungry. So, Allah sent upon them some amazing things. Allah sent clouds to shade them. Then Allah sent upon them a special substance called Manna which was a sweet dish. They could make several things out of it which had immense nutritional value. Also, Allah sent upon them Salwa, which is a type of bird that they could eat.

verses.text: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy (Firaun); We fixed a time to grant you the Tawrat on the right side of Mount Tur and We sent down to you Manna (sweet dish) and Salwa (quail meat) saying : “Eat of the good things We have provided for your sustenance and do not transgress (Surah TaHa : 80 – 81)
We even provided you the shade of clouds and sent down to you al Manna and al Salwa saying: “Eat of the good things, We have provided you” (Surah Al-Baqarah : 57)

points.text: On their way, they passed by a tribe who were worshiping idols. The people said to Musa and Haroon, to make for them idols similar to how these people have. Musa became angry over his people that after witnessing so many of the signs, they were still bent upon shirk and worshiping things apart from Allah. This incident is captured in Surah Al-Araf as below:

verses.text: We made the Children of Israel cross the Red Sea. On their way they came across people who were worshipping their idols. (Surah Al-A’raf : 138)

They said: “O Musa, fashion for us a god like the gods of these people.” Musa replied : “You are indeed very ignorant people. What these people are following is doomed to destruction and their deeds are in vain” (Surah Al-A’raf : 138 – 139).

story.introduction: Appointment at Mount Tur:

points.text: While Musa and Haroon were leading the six to seven hundred thousand people across the desert towards Mount Tur, Musa decided to hurry and reach Mount Tur sooner in order to please Allah. He put Haroon (a.s) in charge of the Children of Israel and rushed to Mount Tur

He had assumed that his people will soon follow him to the Mount. When Musa (a.s) reached to Mount Tur, Allah spoke to him directly. The communion at Mount Tur was supposed to be for thirty nights, but Allah added a further 10 nights to make it 40 nights for communion with his Rabb.

verses.text: We summoned Musa to the mount of Tur for thirty nights and added ten more to complete the term of forty nights for communion with his Rabb. (Surah Al-A’raf : 142)
Musa said to his brother Haroon : “You will be in my place among my people; set a good example and do not follow the way of mischief-makers”. (Surah Al-A’raf : 142)

When Musa came to Mount Tur, Allah said: “But, why have you come with such a haste ahead of your people, O Musa?” He replied: “They are close behind me, I hastened to You O my Rabb, so that You may be pleased”. (Surah Ta-Ha: 83)

points.text: Musa asks that Allah show Himself and the dialogue and happenings are captured in the below ayahs. The Tawrat is revealed to Musa and is given as a written scripture carved into planks of rocks.

verses.text: When Musa came to our appointed place and his Rabb spoke to him, he asked: “O my Rabb! Show me Yourself, that I may look at You.” Allah answered: “You cannot see Me. Look at the mountain; if it remains in its place then you will see Me.” (Surah Al-A’raf : 143)

When his Rabb manifested to the mountain, He crushed it into fine dust and Musa fell down unconscious. When Musa recovered, he said: “Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance and I am the first of the believers”. (Surah Al-A’raf : 143)

We inscribed for him upon tablets all kind of instructions and details of everything, concerning all branches of life, and said: “Observe these with firmness and enjoin your people to follow them according to the best of their abilities (Surah Al-A’raf : 145)

points.text: Allah informs to Musa that his people have transgressed while Musa had rushed to Mount Tur. The Samiriyy has made a calf from the jewellery that the people had with them and they have started to worship it.

verses.text: Allah said: “Well listen! We tested your people after you and the As-Samiriy has led them astray.” (Surah Ta-Ha : 85)

story.introduction: Musa returns from Mount Tur:

verses.text: When Musa came back to his people, he was extremely angry and sorrowful, and he said: “What an evil thing you have done in my absence!” (Surah Al-A’raf : 150)

He put down the Holy Tablets and seized his brother Haroon by the hair of his head and dragged him closer. Haroon cried: “O son of my mother! The people overpowered me and almost killed me; do not make my enemies happy over me and do not count me among the wrongdoers.” (Surah Al-A’raf : 150)

story.introduction: Musa (a.s)’s address to his people:

verses.text: Musa said: “O my people! Did your Rabb not make a gracious promise to you? Did my absence seem too long to you? (Surah Ta-Ha : 86)

The people replied: “We broke the promise although it was no fault of ours. We were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of Firaun’s people and cast them into the fire, and that was what the Samiriyy suggested”. (Surah Ta-Ha : 87)
Then he forged a calf in the shape of a body which produced a mooing sound. Th en he said: “Th is is your god and the god of Musa, but Musa forgot to mention it to you”. (Surah Ta-Ha : 88)

story.introduction: Musa (a.s)’s address to Samiriyy:

verses.text: Musa turned to Samiriyy: “Now what do you have to say about this, O Samiriyy?” (Surah Ta-Ha : 94)

He replied: “I saw what they did not see; so, I took a handful of dust from the track of the Rasool (angel Gabriel) and threw it into the casting of the calf; thus did my soul prompt me.” (Surah Ta-Ha : 95)
Musa cursed him: “Get out of here! Now throughout your life,you will say to other people: ‘Touch me not’; and you will not escape your appointed doom. (Surah Ta-Ha : 96)

story.introduction: Musa orders the killing of people involved in the incident of Golden Calf:

verses.text: Turning to his people, Musa said: “O my people! You have indeed grievously wronged yourselves by taking the calf for worship; so turn in repentance to your Creator and slay the culprits among you; that will be best for you in His sight” (Surah Al-Baqarah: 54)

(It is reported from the Tawrat that the punishment met upon the people was that every tribe will slay among its own people those who were involved in the building and worshiping of the golden calf. There were a total of 12 tribes and it is reported that about 70,000 people were killed as a punishment for this wrong). (Sources: Lectures from Tafsir of Quran by Dr Israar Ahmed)

story.introduction: Destroying the Golden Calf:

points.text: After executing Allah’s command to slay the culprits for taking the calf for worship, Musa (a.s) addressed his people:

verses.text: Behold this god to whom you had become a devoted worshipper: we will burn it and scatter its ashes into the sea”. (Surah Ta-Ha : 96)
Musa further said: “O my people! Your God is only Allah, there is none worthy of worship but He. His knowledge encompasses everything.” (Surah Ta-Ha : 97)

story.introduction: Tawrat and lifting up of Mount Tur:

verses.text: When Musa’s anger calmed down, he took up the Holy Tablets in whose writings there was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Rabb. (Surah Al-A’raf : 154)

points.text: While some of the people from the Children of Israel were willing to accept the Tawrat as brought down by Musa, there were some who demanded that they will first see what is written in the Torah and will accept it only if it suits them. The people felt that the commandments in the Torah would be too heavy for them, and they did not want to implement all of it. So, Allah raised the Mount Tur over them.

verses.text: Reminder is made of the incident when Allah lifted the mount Tur, and commanded the people to hold firm to the Torah and follow the commandments, so that they may become pious. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
We lifted the Mount Tur over them and took the covenant from them that they will obey Our commandments. (Surah An-Nisa : 153)

points.text: After seeing this miracle of the Mount Tur on top of them, all of the people from the Children of Israel agree to abide by the commandments of the Torah.

story.introduction: Musa takes some of his people to Mount Tur:

points.text: Some people from among the Children of Israel had a doubt as to whether Musa (a.s) was really speaking to Allah. So, they went to their leaders and told them to accompany Musa when he goes to Mount Tur and to see if Allah is really speaking to him.

The leaders came to Musa, and explained that witnessing the event will make their message even stronger. Musa chose 70 men from his people who were considered the most pious of them to accompany him to Mount Tur.

Once they reached the place of Allah’s meeting, Musa asked them to stay a little behind while he enters into the Holy Valley. The people could hear the conversation between Musa and Allah. However, when Musa returns back to them, they said that they will not go back unless they see Allah with their own eyes.

Allah sends His anger over them and a violent earthquake kills them all. Musa then sits there, making duas to Allah seeking for their forgiveness and pleading that it was a mistake committed by some fools amongst them. This incident is captured in verses of Surah Al A’raf and Surah Al-Baqarah.

verses.text: Musa chose seventy men from his people to accompany him to Our place of meeting. On their way when they were seized by a violent earthquake, he said: “O my Rabb! Had it been Your will, You could have destroyed them and me long ago. Would you destroy us for some offence committed by some fools among us? (Surah Al-A’raf : 155)
You are our guardian, therefore, forgive us and have mercy on us; for You are the best of all forgivers!” (Surah Al-A’raf : 155)
Remember, when you said: “O Musa! We shall never believe you until we see Allah with our own eyes.”. A thunderbolt struck you while you were looking on and you fell dead. (Surah Al-Baqarah : 55)
Then We raised you up after your death; so that you may be grateful. (Surah Al-Baqarah : 55)

points.text: Musa and the 70 men pleaded forgiveness from Allah and returned back to their people. When they returned, many of the Children of Israel believed in them, and many of them were still weak in their faith.

story.introduction: Allah assigns the Holy Land to the Children of Israel

points.text: The Children of Israel were living in tents in the wilderness of Paran.The Paran is a desert area lying in the Sinai Peninsula adjacent to the northern borders of Arabia and the southern borders of Palestine.

Allah assigned the holy Land of Palestine to the Children of Israel, and this land was the homeland of Ibraheem, Ishaaq and Yaqub (a.s).When they got close to Palestine, Musa and Haroon said to his people to enter the land that has been written for you.But the people refused to enter saying that a nation of giants live there.The people disobeyed and went to the extent of asking Musa,Haroon and their Rabb to go and fight, and once they remove them, they will enter the land.The incidents are beautifully captured in Surah Al-Ma’idah as below.

verses.text: And Musa said to his people: “O my people! Enter into the holy land which Allah has assigned for you. Do not turn back, because if you do, you will become losers”. (Surah Al-Ma’idah : 21)
They said : “O Musa! A nation of giants live in there, we will not set our foot in it until they leave. As soon as they leave, we will be ready to enter”. (Surah Al-Ma’idah : 22)

Ther eupon two Allah fearing men (Musa and Haroon) upon whom Allah had bestowed His Grace said: “Attack directly at the city gate, once you enter it, you will surely be victorious. Put your trust in Allah if you are really believers”. (Surah Al-Ma’idah : 23)
The people replied: “O Musa! We will never enter it so long as they remain therein. Therefore, both you and your Rabb should go and fight, we will stay here” (Surah Al-Ma’idah : 24)
Hearing this Musa and Haroon prayed: O my Rabb! I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother. Please, set us apart from these disobedient people.” (Surah Al-Ma’idah : 25)

Allah responded: “Very well, they are forbidden from this land for forty years; during this time they will wander homeless on the earth, so do not grieve for these disobedient people”. (Surah Al Ma’idah : 26)

story.introduction: The Lost Generation

points.text: Forty years of wandering meant that the whole generation of people would be lost and without a place which that can call as home. Allah kept sending down to them Manna and Salwa. But the people had got tired of the same things to eat and demanded some other foods. Also, when the people were thirsty, they came to Musa asking him to pray to Allah for water. These incidents are captured in the below verses of Surah Al-Baqarah.

verses.text: Remember, when Musa prayed for water for his people. Allah said: “Strike the rock with your staff”. (Surah Al-Baqarah : 60)
There upon twelve springs came out of it. Each tribe was assigned its own drinking place. (Surah Al-Baqarah : 60)

Remember, when you said: “O Musa! We cannot endure one kind of food; call upon your Rabb to give us a variety of food which the earth produces, such as green-herbs, cucumbers, garlic, lentils and onions” (Surah Al-Baqarah : 61)
“What” Musa asked. “Would you exchange the better for the worse? (Surah Al-Baqarah : 61)

points.text: Musa warned his people for not being grateful and told them that if that is what they want, they can settle down to a city and they will find these foods.

As a result of the Children of Israel continuously rejecting the commandments of Allah, being ungrateful for the blessings bestowed upon them and transgressing beyond bounds, the wrath of Allah fell upon them, as Allah says:

verses.text: Gradually they became so degraded that shame and misery were brought upon them and they drew upon themselves the wrath of Allah; this was because they kept on rejecting the commandments of Allah and killed His prophets unjustly, furthermore, it was the consequence of their disobedience and transgression. (Surah-Al Baqarah : 61)

story.text: There are two important stories from the time of Musa which we will cover today In sha Allah. One, is the story of Musa (a.s) and Khizr (a.s). The other story is of a man who was murdered from among the Children of Israel and Allah’s command to slaughter a cow.

story.introduction: Introduction

verses.text: Now tell them about the story of Khizr to whom Allah has given special knowledge. Musa (a.s) was asked to go to him and learn from him. (From Surah Al-Kahf)

Musa set out on the journey with a young servant. They reached the junction of the two seas, when the fish they were carrying miraculously made its way into the river and disappeared. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 9)

They had passed some distance when Musa said to his young servant that they have suffered much fatigue and they should have their meal. At that moment, the servant boy recalled about the fish having made its way into the river. He blamed that it was only Shaitan who made him to forget to mention about this incident to Musa. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 9)
They retraced their steps back to the place, and there they found Khizr, whom Allah had blessed with special knowledge. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 9)
Musa requested to Khizr: “May I follow you so that you may teach me from the True Knowledge which you have been taught”. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 9)
Khizr warned that Musa would not be patient enough to understand his actions, but Musa insisted. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 9)
An agreement was reached that Musa should not question Khizr for any of his actions, until Khizr himself mentions about it to Musa. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 9)
Khizr and Musa embarked on a boat and Khizr made a hole in it. Musa questions why he did such a weird thing and it will only drown its passengers. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)
Khizr warned Musa for questioning his action and Musa immediately apologizes. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

They journey on until they meet a boy and Khizr kills him. Musa says: “You have killed an innocent person though he had killed nobody. Surely, you have done a horrible thing!” (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

Khizr reminds Musa about their agreement, that Musa would not question his actions. Musa pleads: “If ever I ask you about anything after this, you may not keep me in your company”. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

They travel on and come to a town and ask for food, but the people of the town refuse to receive them as their guests. They find a wall there on the point of falling down, and Khizr restores it. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)
Musa wonders and asks Khizr: “If you wanted you could have taken some wages for it! (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)
Khizr says: “That’s it; this is the parting between you and me. But first I will explain to you those acts of mine which you could not bear to watch with patience.” (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)
Khizr explains that the damage he did to the boat was to prevent a king on the other side, who was seizing boats by force from the poor fishermen. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

As for the youth that Khizr killed, his parents were true believers, and the boy was a rebel and a disbeliever. Allah would grant to the parents, a son more righteous and better in affection. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

As for the wall, it belonged to 2 orphan boys and beneath it their treasure was buried. Since their father was a righteous man, Allah desired that the treasure be protected and the children should take it after they reach maturity. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

Khizr says: “All this was done as a mercy by your Rabb. What I did was not done by my own will. This is the interpretation of those actions which you could not bear to watch with patience. (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 10)

story.introduction: Incident of the Murdered Man and Allah’s command to Slaughter a Cow

points.text: During the time of the Lost Generation, the people were forbidden to enter the holy land for forty years. There came an incident wherein someone from the Children of Israel had killed a man. The people started to dispute among one another as to who killed him. The matter was brough to Musa and Musa informed that Allah commands you to sacrifice a cow.

The significance of this command can be understood in light of the background that during the time of Firaun, the people used to worship idols and many gods. Among them, the people worshipped a male calf which was made out of gold and also a female cow which was bigger. There was the superstition that the female cow had godly characteristics and to slaughter a female cow meant that it was bad luck for everyone. Allah wanted to test the people and break this false belief among them.

In their reluctance to slaughter the Cow, the people kept asking more and more details of the Cow which made it more difficult for them and showed how they were in denial to the command of Allah. This incident is captured in Surah Al-Baqarah as below.

verses.text: Reminder of the incident, when Musa (a.s) said to his people: “Allah commands you to sacrifice a cow”. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
The people said: “Request your Rabb to give some details of that cow. Musa replied: “Allah says, the cow should neither be too old or too young but of middle age.  (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
The people asked again: “Clarify for us her color”. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
Musa replied: “Allah says, the said cow should be of a rich and deep yellow color, pleasing to the eyes”. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
The people said: “Request your Rabb to clarify for us the exact type of cow she should be, because to us all cows look alike”.  (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
Musa replied: “Allah says, the said cow should have neither been used to till the soil nor water the fields; a healthy one, free from blemish with no spot on her.  (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)
The people finally said: “Now you have brought us the accurate description”. They slaughtered the cow, after they had almost declined.  (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 8)

story.introduction: Murder of a man from among the Children of Israel

points.text: Coming to the incident of the murdered man, it is narrated in Surah Al-Baqarah

verses.text: When you killed a man and started disputing as to who killed him, Allah made it known what you concealed. (Surah AlBaqarah : Section 9)
So, We said: “Strike the dead body with a piece of the slaughtered cow”. Thus, Allah brought the dead to life and showed you His Signs so that you may understand.  (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 9)
